summary: Okanogan NF site of a 1930s camp with a platform tower, abandoned in the 1940s; no remains described, reached by a 1.3-mile hike from FR 100.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1940s; the sources describe no remains at the site
facts.agency: Okanogan National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

access.note: On Okanogan National Forest land, reached on foot from a pass on FR 100 where there is parking. Willhite notes a sign asking visitors to close a gate after entering.

visit.trail_note: Park at the pass on FR 100, reached from the Twisp River Road by Little Bridge Creek Road and about 3 miles of gravel. The hike is 1.3 miles with 550 feet of gain (Willhite).

corrections.why: The register's Built field reads 1930's, which is a decade rather than a single year. The record's 1930 is more precise than the source.

sources.title: Two Forest Service fire guards become the first smokejumpers to parachute into a forest fire in Washington on August 10, 1940

notes_for_editor: Build and abandonment dates are decades only, so the events carry the decade start with a note. HistoryLink describes a 1939 ground-fought fire and the 1940 smokejumper jump at Little Bridge Creek; no source ties either to this lookout, and the story says so. No source describes what remains at the site. Willhite has no pictures or maps of the site, and no new photos were found.
